newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PLYMOUTH, CHESTERFIELD FINED FOR MATCH BRAWL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PLYMOUTH, CHESTERFIELD FINED FOR MATCH BRAWL.

text.p: Second division clubs Plymouth Argyle and Chesterfield have been fined for a match brawl in February in which five players were sent off, the clubs said on Friday.

Plymouth were fined a total of 30,000 pounds ($48,800) with 22,500 pounds suspended until June 15 next year, while the penalty for Chesterfield was 20,000 pounds with 15,000 pounds suspended, the Football Association ruled at a hearing on Thursday.
The clubs must pay the residual 7,500 and 5,000 pounds within 14 days.

"We have to behave next season or the other amount will become due. We don't like being fined but equally we regret the occasion and will be ensuring it doesn't happen again," Plymouth chief executive Roger Matthews said.
Two players from each side were sent off after an incident sparked by a foul on Plymouth goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar. Plymouth team mate Ronnie Mauge had already been shown the red card.
